# Wicked Campaigns (cv-wicked-campaigns)

> This file documents Wicked Campaigns for AI assistants: Foundry modules such as
> **Pseudo (cv-pseudo)** read a module's root `llms.txt` to answer the table's how-to questions
> about it. It is reference documentation, not configuration — humans are welcome to read it too.

A campaign management and helper module for Foundry VTT V14. Its centrepiece is the **Session Zero
card game**: a deck of prompt cards the table works through together to build characters and the
fiction around them before play starts. Around that sit a Lifepath wizard, a Chase tracker, a Drama
(social conflict) tracker, NPC Motives, and a Fate Pool.

Requires: `campaign-codex`, `complete-card-management` (CCM), `tagger`, `monks-active-tiles`,
`dice-so-nice`. Recommends `lib-wrapper`.

## The Session Zero card game

The deck lives on the canvas, on CCM's **Cards layer** (the card icon in the left-hand scene
controls; `Alt+Z` toggles between Tokens and Cards). Almost every control is on a **right-click
HUD** — right-click the deck for deck controls, right-click a dealt card for card controls.

**The scene needs a discard pile.** CCM's per-scene "canvas pile" is where dealt cards actually
go. The shipped adventure wires this up already; a hand-built scene must set it or dealing breaks.

### Deck controls (right-click the deck, GM only)

| Control | What it does |
|---|---|
| Discard by Suit | Send every remaining card of one suit to the discard pile |
| Keystone Cards | Mark the clearest example of each card type — see below |
| Refresh from Compendium | Replace this world's cards with the shipped version |
| Draw a Card | Deal a specific card, wherever it sits in the deck |
| Return All Cards to Deck | Clear the table; every card goes back to its place |
| Start / End Session Zero | Begin or finish a recorded game |
| Draw Arcana | *(during a game)* Deal the closing Arcana card |
| Reset Deck | Recall everything and re-stack in draw order |

### Card controls (right-click a dealt card)

Everyone gets **View Card Image** (a zoomable viewer) and **Open Session Notes**. The GM also gets
**Record Answer**. **Roll d8 for Other Players** and **Return to Deck** are available as relevant.

### Draw order

Reset stacks the deck as: **theme** (by value) → **skulls** → **moons/mobius/roses** shuffled
together → **major arcana** last. The Arcana are the most open-ended cards in the deck, so they are
deliberately the closer, asked once the fiction is established.

### Keystone cards

A keystone is the clearest, most idiot-proof example of its card type. Mark several candidates per
suit, and each Reset promotes one at random to be the first card of that suit the table sees — so
players always learn a type from its best example, while the GM still gets a different opening each
run. Marking is per-card and survives a Refresh from Compendium.

### Card types and their procedures

| Suit | Procedure |
|---|---|
| Skulls | Add a truth to a villain |
| Moons | One answer for the whole group; you must reach agreement |
| Mobius | Everyone answers, clockwise from whoever drew the card |
| Roses | A relationship between two PCs; capped per player |
| Major Arcana | The drawing player reads it and says how it fits their character |
| Theme | The fixed opener that sets the table |

Each card also prints its own procedure on its face.

### Limits and auto-thinning

Starting a game asks for per-tier limits (villain, Arcana per player, moons, mobius, roses per
player). When a tier hits its limit, the GM is offered the chance to discard the rest of that suit,
which is what keeps a session to roughly 18–30 cards. **Declining those prompts makes the session
much longer** and pushes the Arcana far back — use Draw Arcana if you want the closer regardless.

### The shared record

Answers are recorded into a **Session Zero Summary** journal. It opens shared with the table:
players can read every recorded answer and **append their own notes** to any of them, threaded
under the answer they respond to and signed by the Foundry user who wrote them. Player notes are
relayed through the active GM rather than written directly, so simultaneous notes cannot overwrite
each other. Summaries created before this feature existed show a **Share with Table** button.

Recording a card's headline answer stays with the GM, because that is what moves the tier counters.

### The game tracker

A tracker window shows whose turn it is and how many of each card type the table has spent. The GM
can drag to reorder turns, step turns, and end the session; players get a live read-only copy.

### Player access

Players need **Observer** on the deck and on the scene's discard pile to use any of this. Starting
a game grants that automatically. Observer is deliberate: players can open the card HUD, zoom cards
and roll the d8, but cannot drag, rotate, flip, re-sort or delete anything on the table.

## Other features

- **Lifepath Wizard** — roll or pick a character's background from linked tables; saves into a
  Campaign Codex backstory entry.
- **Chase Tracker** — DMG chase rules with per-terrain complication tables, dash counting against
  a Constitution threshold, and a player HUD.
- **Drama Tracker** — structured social conflicts, with a GM panel and player HUD.
- **NPC Motives** — trackable motive values that can be shown on token bars.
- **Fate Pool** — a shared pool with keybindings to add and spend points.
- **Card Image Viewer** — a zoomable, pannable image viewer that (with `lib-wrapper`) replaces
  Foundry's native image popout everywhere.

## Settings

`sessionZeroEnabled`, `chaseTrackerEnabled`, `dramaEnabled`, `motivesEnabled`, `fatePoolEnabled`,
`lifepathWizardEnabled`, `cardImageViewerEnabled`, `inameTheeIntegration`. Feature toggles are
world-scoped; turning one off hides its UI entirely.

## Keybindings

`Alt+Z` toggle Tokens/Cards layer · `Alt+M` dictate into the Record Answer editor · plus bindings
for the Fate Pool (add/spend/manage) and for opening Chase and Drama setup.

## Compendiums

`wicked-adventures` (the Queen of Storms card game scene, deck and discard pile — import this to
get a working table), `wicked-lore`, `wicked-roll-tables` (Lifepath and chase tables),
`wicked-macros`, `wicked-scenes`, `wicked-actors`, `wicked-example-characters`, `wicked-items`,
`wicked-playlists`.

## Common questions

**A player right-clicks a card and nothing happens.** They lack Observer on the stack the card is
currently in — usually the discard pile rather than the deck. Start a Session Zero game, which
grants both, or set it by hand on the Cards documents.

**Cards vanish when dealt / the deck seems to shrink.** Dealing from a deck keeps the original in
the deck marked "drawn" and puts a copy in the destination. The deck's card count never changes;
its *available* count does. Return to Deck or Reset undoes this.

**The deck has old art or old card names after an update.** A world keeps the copy it imported.
Use **Refresh from Compendium** on the deck.

**A card was dealt by mistake.** Right-click it → Return to Deck. To clear everything, use Return
All Cards to Deck on the deck itself.
